With `all: true`, it returns every map's pins instead, cities included, from the game's map files (`maps`: each map's `tag`, `file` and `pins` with `name`, `tag` and `area`). This works from anywhere and tells you which map a pin is on, but shows each pin's starting state, not its current one.

all.description: Return every map's pins, cities included, from the game's files (starting states) instead of the open map. Default false.

topics.description: A creature began a clip on its base layer, by the engine's own play call: a command's step (a swing, an evade, a deathblow, a knockdown), a conversation line, a walk, the idle. Clips the animation set starts on its own (a one-shot returning to the idle) are not seen. Often several a second in a fight: read it with `match` on the creature's id or tag.

fields.row: the animation's row of the animations table (anim_base, anim_combat, anim_placeables), a number
fields.label: the row's Label
fields.blend: the fade into it, in weight per second; -1 instant, -2 over a fifth of the clip
fields.flag: the play call's last argument, as the engine passes it
fields.position: where the creature stood, [x, y, z]

topics.description: An area finished loading: the party is placed in it and its load scripts have run. Once per load, a save's own load aside (that is eluvian.game.loaded).
A creature's command ended. `result` says how.

fields.playerIssued: whether the player gave the command
fields.target: the same as when it started
fields.point: the same as when it started
fields.ability: the same as when it started
fields.result: how it ended: success, a COMMAND_FAILED_* code saying why it failed, or cleared (dropped from the queue before it finished)

topics.description: A creature started a command from its queue: an attack, a move, an ability, a wait, an animation, and so on.

fields.type: the kind of command (Attack, MoveToObject, UseAbility, ...)
fields.playerIssued: whether the player gave the command
fields.target: the object it acts on, for an attack, a use or a move to an object, if any
fields.point: the [x, y, z] point it moves to or aims at, for a move or an ability, if any
fields.ability: the ability's id, for a UseAbility

topics.description: A creature died, or a party member fell, on the frame its health reached 0: any creature. The engine's own eluvian.script.death fires about 2 seconds later, once the death has played out.

fields.killer: who killed it: the death's own creator, else the last creature to hurt it; null for `stage_kill`'s, whose damage comes from no one

topics.description: The player is offered replies, listed in the order shown on screen.

fields.replies: each reply with its position, index, text and icon

topics.description: An item was put on a creature, by any means: the inventory screen, `equip`, or a script. It does not fire when equipping is refused, nor for the ammunition the engine gives each creature when an area loads.

fields.slotName: the slot's name, as `inventory` names it

topics.description: An item was taken off a creature, by any means. When equipping one item pushes another out (a shield, for a two-handed weapon), the pushed-out item's event comes first.

topics.description: A save finished loading, or a new game started, and the world is ready.

topics.description: The game takes the player's input again: explore or combat entered from another mode (a load, a conversation, a cutscene, a screen).

topics.description: The game started a sound: an FMOD event, by the event's own start, so music, the interface, footsteps, blows, voices and ambience alike. Often many a second: read it with `match` on the path, or a part of the path's own field. Which creature made it is not known.

fields.path: the event's path, "project/group/.../event", as the scripts' PlaySound names it
fields.name: the event's own name, the path's last part
fields.positional: true for a sound placed in the world (FMOD's 3-D mode); false for music and the interface
fields.position: where it was placed, [x, y, z], for a positional sound; a 3-D sound nobody placed yet is at its default, usually the origin
